64	static uint64_t magicmem[8] __attribute__((aligned(64)));
65	
66	/* The host (SimControl) reads magicmem straight from RAM, behind the
67	 * hart's caches, so write back L1 (and L2 if present) before handing the
68	 * command over. CCTL command 6 = L1D_WBINVAL_ALL, 0x12 = L2_WBINVAL_ALL.
69	 * On QEMU the CSR write is accepted and memory is coherent anyway. */
70	static void flush_dcache(void)
71	{
72	  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));
73	#if __riscv_xlen == 64
74	  /* L2 writeback, gated to rv64 because it uses rv64-only ld/sd to reach the
75	   * 64-bit L2C MMIO registers (mmsc_cfg bit 46 is the L2-present flag) -- it
76	   * cannot COMPILE on rv32. Whether to flush is still decided at runtime by the
77	   * bit-46 check inside the asm. An rv32 core WITH an L2C would need a
78	   * 32-bit-halves access path here; today's rv32 target (d23) has no L2, so the
79	   * L1 writeback above suffices. */
80	  __asm__ __volatile__(
81	    "csrr    t0, mmsc_cfg\n"
82	    "li      t1, 1\n"
83	    "slli    t1, t1, 46\n"
84	    "and     t2, t0, t1\n"
85	    "beqz    t2, 1f\n"
86	    "li      t3, 0xe0500008\n"   /* L2C_REG_CTL: enabled? */
87	    "ld      t4, 0(t3)\n"
88	    "andi    t4, t4, 1\n"
89	    "beqz    t4, 1f\n"
90	    "li      t5, 0xe0500040\n"   /* L2C_REG_CCTL <- WBINVAL_ALL */
91	    "li      t6, 0x12\n"
92	    "sd      t6, 0(t5)\n"
93	    "2:\n"
94	    "li      t2, 0xe0500080\n"   /* poll L2C_REG_CCTL_M0_ST until idle */
95	    "ld      t3, 0(t2)\n"
96	    "andi    t3, t3, 0xF\n"
97	    "li      t5, 1\n"
98	    "beq     t3, t5, 2b\n"
99	    "1:\n" ::: "t0", "t1", "t2", "t3", "t4", "t5", "t6", "memory");
100	#endif
101	}

103	static intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uintptr_t a0, uintptr_t a1,
104	                             uintptr_t a2, uintptr_t a3)
105	{
106	  magicmem[0] = n;
107	  magicmem[1] = a0;
108	  magicmem[2] = a1;
109	  magicmem[3] = a2;
110	  magicmem[4] = a3;
111	  magicmem[5] = 0;
112	  magicmem[6] = 0;
113	  magicmem[7] = 0;
114	  flush_dcache();
115	  *(volatile uint64_t*) HTIF_TOHOST_CMD = (uintptr_t) magicmem;
116	  __asm__ __volatile__("fence rw,rw" ::: "memory");
117	  return (intptr_t) magicmem[0];

input.description: Check for MMIO replay in hybrid layer and QEMU L2C model

content.text:
No - andesim does not transport MMIO device state today, and there is no automatic way to "copy" QEMU's MMIO writes into vsim. The handoff moves exactly two things: hart architectural state (`hybrid_state_v1`: GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V/PMP/Andes block) and RAM (the /dev/shm shared mmap). Device registers are inside each simulator's own device model, so whatever QEMU wrote stays in QEMU; vsim's devices start at RTL reset.

Whether you must re-set a region in vsim depends on which of 3 cases it falls in:

**1. Devices vsim does not decode at all - most of the AE350 map.**
vsim's platform maps only: RAM, ILM/DLM, ACM, AIA IF, SimControl (0xE0080000), Debug Module, SMU, UART1/UART2 (`vsim_andesim/src/platform/memory_map.h`). PLIC, PLMT, PIT, WDT, RTC, GPIO, DMAC, etc. do not exist in vsim. You cannot transport them, and you don't need to: their config only matters for the QEMU phase. The ROI is trap-free and interrupt-free by contract, so PLIC/PLMT setup is irrelevant inside the window. The only rule: ROI code must never touch these addresses - in vsim they are unmapped and the access would fault.

**2. Devices both engines model and the ROI uses live.**
UART2 (printf) and SimControl/HTIF already work: the ROI's own loads/stores go straight to the vsim model. Their QEMU-phase register config is not copied, but today's vsim models don't depend on it.

**3. Device config that changes ROI timing - the L2C register block (0xE0500000) is the canonical case.**
This is the same problem as `mcache_ctl` (L1 enable), but through MMIO instead of a CSR, so the existing CSR transport does NOT cover it. Right now it is moot:

- The shipped engine has no L2: `Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc` says `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB 0`, so `has_shared_cache = false` and the core reports mmsc_cfg.L2C=0 (the vplat runtime already guards its L2C access on that bit, `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:86`).
- QEMU's "L2C" at 0xE0500000 is only a writable RAM stub (`memory_region_init_ram`, `qemu_andesim/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1492`) - no function, and it is private QEMU RAM, not part of the shared mmap, so its contents don't survive the handoff either.

For a future engine built WITH an L2C, yes - the enable/config writes from the QEMU phase would have to be replayed into vsim, or the window runs with L2 at reset (off) and the cycle figure inflates, exactly like the mcache_ctl story. The natural mechanism: vsim resumes exactly at the ROI entry, so the program itself has no chance to redo device init; the injection point is `ResumeDriver` - replay a small whitelist of MMIO registers via Program-Buffer store instructions before `dret` (the same machinery the V-scratch sweep uses), with the QEMU side draining those values into the handoff. That is a design extension, not something in the code today.
